question: What proof must alumni provide when applying for an RMIT Alumni card?
expected_answer: Alumni must prove that they have completed degree programs at RMIT at the time of application. An alumni card will only be granted when appropriate proof of status is presented.
expected_context: When applying for Alumni card, proof of status will be required. You have to prove that you've completed degree programs at the time you apply for alumni card. An alumni card will only be granted when appropriate proof of status is presented.

question: Is there an expiration date on the RMIT Alumni card?
expected_answer: No, there is no expiration date for the alumni card no matter when the alumnus graduated.
expected_context: There is no expiration date for alumni card no matter when you graduated.

question: Can alumni request a reprint of their Alumni card if it is lost or broken?
expected_answer: Yes, alumni can request a reprint with no fee charge. However, they cannot do so within the first year of their first card request.
expected_context: You can request to reprint your alumni card in case of loss or breakage with no fee charge. However, you cannot do so within the first year of your first card request.

question: What happens if another person uses your Alumni card to access RMIT facilities?
expected_answer: The Alumni card is non-transferable. If another individual uses your card to attempt to gain access to the facility, RMIT University reserves the right to terminate your Alumni card.
expected_context: Alumni card is non-transferable: should another individual use your card to attempt to gain access to the facility, RMIT University reserves the right to terminate your Alumni card.

question: What is the minimum age for children to enter RMIT indoor facilities?
expected_answer: Children under the age of 13 are not permitted to enter the indoor facilities unless they are to be supervised by a responsible person whilst taking part in any on-campus activities.
expected_context: Children under the age of 13 are not permitted to enter the indoor facilities unless they are to be supervised by a responsible person whilst taking part in any on-campus activities.

question: How much does the REC membership cost for alumni per semester?
expected_answer: Entire semester (Week 1 – Week 17): VND 900,000. Half of the semester (Week 1 – Week 9 or Week 9 – Week 17): VND 450,000.
expected_context: The REC membership fee for Alumni is based on a semester-by-semester basis: Entire semester (Week 1 – Week 17): VND 900,000. Half of the semester (Week 1 – Week 9 or Week 9-Week 17): VND 450,000.

question: What are the REC operational hours for alumni members?
expected_answer: Mondays to Saturdays: 6.00 – 21.00. Sundays: 9.00 – 18.00. University / public holidays: closed.
expected_context: REC operational hours: Mondays to Saturdays: 6.00 – 21.00. Sundays: 9.00 – 18.00. University / public holidays: closed.

question: What alternative identification can a registered alumnus present if they forget their RMIT Alumni card at the REC?
expected_answer: A government ID card (i.e. Chứng Minh Nhân Dân or Thẻ Căn Cước Công Dân) or driving license should be presented.
expected_context: In the event that a registered alumnus forgets his/her RMIT alumni card, a government ID card (i.e. Chứng Minh Nhân Dân or Thẻ Căn Cước Công Dân) or driving license should be presented.

question: How many booking slots can one student ID reserve at once for library study rooms?
expected_answer: 1 ID can book a maximum of 2 slots at once, with a maximum time of 60 minutes per 1 slot.
expected_context: RULES AND POLICIES: 1 ID can book a maximum of 2 slots at once. Maximum time per 1 slot: 60 minutes.

question: How far in advance can students book a study room, and when will the booking be automatically canceled?
expected_answer: Students can only book for 2 weeks in advance (14 days). The booking will be canceled 15 minutes after the scheduled time if no ID is received at the front desk.
expected_context: Students can only book for 2 weeks in advance (14 days). The booking will be canceled 15 minutes after the scheduled time if no ID is received at the front desk.

question: What is the maximum percentage of a book that can be used as a snippet or quote under copyright guidelines?
expected_answer: Not more than 1% of a work. This applies to 1% of the number of pages of a publication totalling more than 200 pages, 1% of pages in a paginated electronic work (PDF), or 1% of words of an electronic work that is not paginated.
expected_context: Using snippets or quotes from books is fine as long as the quote taken is within reasonable limits, that is not quoting more than what would be considered 1% of a work (1% of the number of pages of a publication totalling more than 200 pages, 1% of pages in a paginated electronic work [PDF], or 1% of words of an electronic work that is not paginated).

question: How much of a book can students scan or print under fair dealing provisions for research and study?
expected_answer: 1 chapter or 10% of the number of pages in the work.
expected_context: Scanning/Printing Limits [how much you can scan or print] – 1 chapter or 10% of the number of pages in the work under fair dealing provisions.

question: Does the American 'Fair Use' concept apply in Australia?
expected_answer: No. Fair use is an American provision and terminology for using copyright works and does not apply in Australia. Australia uses 'fair dealing' provisions instead.
expected_context: Fair use is an American provision and terminology for using copyright works and does not apply in Australia. Australia uses 'fair dealing' provisions instead.

question: What must students do with copyright works placed online after they are no longer enrolled in a course?
expected_answer: Copyright works incorporated into online environments within RMIT such as blogs, e-Portfolios, or other online platforms can only remain online whilst enrolled. If you are no longer enrolled in the course the works must be removed.
expected_context: Copyright works [that are not creative commons or free licensed works], incorporated into online environments within RMIT such as blogs, e-Portfolios, or other online platforms can only remain online whilst enrolled, if you are no longer enrolled in the course the works must be removed.
